title: 2026 APNIC Survey report released
description: The 2026 APNIC Survey report is now available, providing valuable feedback from Members and the wider Internet community on APNIC’s performance, priorities, and future direction.

title: FCC Moves to Open 1,050 MHz of Spectrum to Satellite Broadband
description: The FCC plans to open 1,050 MHz in the 12.7 GHz and 42 GHz bands to expanded satellite use, adding capacity for broadband, mobile connectivity, inter-satellite links and ground networks.

title: ICANN Accountability Without gTLD Remedies Is Just Documentation
description: Past gTLD disputes show applicants can win ICANN accountability rulings without obtaining the contested string, raising a critical question for 2026 applicants about whether expanded review mechanisms can deliver meaningful remedies.

title: How we rebuilt Cloudflare Workers’ module registry for Node.js compatibility
description: Workers now enables Node.js compatibility by default, supports applications up to 64 mebibytes, and adds a URL-based module registry with import.meta, lazy compilation, shared code caches, and clearer errors.

title: APNIC and NIXI partner to strengthen routing security and technical capacity in India
description: The partnership will expand IPv6 and RPKI deployment including piloting an RPKI Repository Mirror to support a more secure and resilient Internet ecosystem.

title: Building resilient self hosted services is not always easy
description: Resiliency through more redundancy is important no matter the scenario.

title: DNS Spotlight: 2026’s 5 Most Notorious Ransomware
description: DNS analysis of 84 network indicators tied to LockBit, Cl0p, Akira, Medusa, and Qilin uncovered thousands of connected domains and IP addresses, including additional artifacts already identified as malicious.

title: G7 Cyber Agencies Urge Immediate Post-Quantum Migration Planning
description: G7 cybersecurity agencies are pressing governments and organizations to inventory cryptographic dependencies and accelerate post-quantum migration as long transition timelines and future quantum attacks threaten Internet security infrastructure.

title: Automatic Key Exchange: faster, post-quantum secure origin handshakes for 45 billion daily connections (and counting)
description: Automatic Key Exchange probes TLS 1.3-capable customer origins to learn which key agreement algorithms they support. We then lead with the most secure algorithm when connecting to the origin, preferring post-quantum connections wherever the origin supports it.

title: The Internet’s New Edge Builders
description: After building private backbones, content and cloud platforms are now moving closer to users. In doing so, they are taking on delivery roles once associated mainly with independent CDNs.

title: Welcome to APNIC 62
description: APNIC welcomes you to Mumbai, India for APNIC 62. Here is what you can look forward to over the coming days.

title: 15th Registration Operations Workshop, September 29, 2026, 13:00 - 17:00 UTC
description: The 15th Registration Operations Workshop convenes domain name and DNS professionals September 29 for technical sessions on mTLS, RPKI, DNS resilience, delegations, DNSSEC, registrar concentration, dispute proceedings and alternative naming systems.

title: WSIS Forum 2026: From commitments to measurable implementation
description: WSIS Forum 2026 marked the start of a new phase for global digital development, shifting the focus from commitments to measurable implementation.

title: When a Link Becomes a Border: The Quiet Geopolitics of Internet Access
description: A LinkedIn short-link anomaly in Iran reveals how sanctions, corporate compliance and geolocation controls can translate geopolitical boundaries into infrastructure-level restrictions, creating an Internet that remains globally connected while becoming functionally unequal.

title: Satellite Collisions Rise as Earth’s Orbits Grow Crowded
description: Rapid satellite growth is raising collision risks as orbital debris accumulates, avoidance maneuvers multiply, and solar storms could disable spacecraft, exposing the absence of effective international governance for increasingly crowded orbits.

title: ICANN Taps Analysys Mason for Key 2026 New gTLD Reviews
description: Analysys Mason will run geographic and reserved-name reviews for ICANN's 2026 new-gTLD round, applying rules that can determine whether proposed strings advance, require government support, qualify for exceptions, or face further evaluation.

title: Canada Sets National Principles for Responsible Data-Centre Development
description: Canada's voluntary framework asks data-center developers to cover electricity-system costs, limit water and environmental impacts, disclose local effects and deliver national benefits as the country expands sovereign AI and cloud infrastructure.

title: Closing the IPv6 First-Packet Gap with GRAND
description: There is a subtle asymmetry in IPv6 Neighbour Discovery: a host knows how to reach its router before the router necessarily knows how to reach the host. GRAND fixes that asymmetry by making the host proactively advertise its address, and I implemented that mechanism in FreeBSD.

title: Community consultation on increasing diversity in APNIC community leadership: Stage 1 report released
description: The APNIC Executive Council has released the Stage 1 report on APNIC’s community consultation on increasing diversity in APNIC community leadership. The discussion will continue at APNIC 62 in Mumbai, with remote participation available.

title: What part of ‘No!’ is so hard for the DNS understand?
description: At APNIC Labs we've been experimenting with understanding how the DNS handles requests to resolve nonexistent names to make the DNS more resilient to random name attacks.

title: Introducing context-aware vulnerability discovery and remediation with Cloudflare Managed Defense and OpenAI Daybreak models
description: Use production traffic and security signals to prioritize findings, prepare edge mitigations when safe, and propose code patches. By combining WAF data with OpenAI Daybreak models, Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation helps teams identify and patch the most critical threats fi…

title: ChatGPT, Claude and Grok Suffer Overlapping Service Outages
description: Overlapping outages disrupted ChatGPT, Claude and Grok on September 3, but their providers have identified no common cause, leaving unanswered whether the failures were coincidental or reflected an unseen shared dependency.

title: Introducing the ARIN 58 Fellows
description: Amanda Gauldin, ARIN Senior Project Manager, shares details about the Fellows, Mentors, and special guests joining us for the ARIN 58 Fellowship Program.

title: When Traceroutes Lie: How TTL Jumps Can Give Us a False Impression of the Internet’s Topology
description: Traceroute is a powerful tool for uncovering how packets travel across the Internet. However, as we recently discovered, some routers tamper with the TTL values in traceroute's probing packets, giving you a false view of how networks are actually interconnected.

title: Spurs boots VMware, cites 85% licensing saving
description: Part of wider infrastructure replacement upgrade project with HPE

title: [Podcast] Measuring the impact of locally served root zone
description: An analysis of the traffic impacts of locally served root zones, by Ilyas Rahimi at UvA.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Theory and Practice in Internet Operations
description: Internet research can benefit from operational insight, and network operators from research expertise. Building on what we learned at RIPE 92, we look at practical ways to make those connections easier and turn promising conversations into lasting collaboration.

title: Beeline: Enforcing application-layer policies in eBPF
description: Guest Post: While many L7 protocols are complex to parse, the logic needed to enforce L7 policies tends to be simple. For the vast majority (89%) of L7 policies in the wild, Beeline can eliminate the service proxy from the critical path.

title: IETF 126 Highlights
description: The IETF 126 meeting was held 18–24 July 2026 at the Hilton Vienna Park in Vienna, Austria, and online, hosted by Cisco. The week included the IETF Hackathon and Code Sprint, the New Participants' Program, five Birds-of-a-Feather (BoF) sessions, and more than 100 working group an…

title: How we could save petabytes of cache storage with Zstandard and Pingora
description: Could we get more cache space with the same hardware? We prototyped compression inside Cloudflare's cache to find out.

title: The IRR Landscape: What RPKI Can Replace
description: In the third part of our IRR landscape series, we use traffic measurements from AMS-IX and DE-CIX to assess which parts of the IRR landscape can safely be replaced with RPKI. Third-party ROUTE(6) objects can largely be phased out, while third-party AS-SETs remain essential for BG…

title: Recommended Draft RIR Governance Document, Rationale report, and next steps
description: The NRO NC has published the Recommended Draft RIR Governance Document, including a redline version and rationale document.

title: Introducing Adaptive Intelligence: Undermining the economics of every bot attack
description: Bot operators have historically had the economic advantage, bypassing static, deterministic detection rules with cheap proxies and retooling. Cloudflare's new Adaptive Intelligence engine flips this dynamic by autonomously learning from the meta-signals of live traffic and deploy…

title: IETF email infrastructure transition planned for 11 September
description: A transition to a new modern, modular, and containerized infrastructure for email services provided for ietf.org, iab.org, irtf.org, rfc-editor.org (including email lists) is scheduled for 11 September 2026 starting at 2200UTC, with message delivery delayed up to 60 minutes. Furt…

title: BotBase for Operators: A clearer path to joining Cloudflare's directory of bots and agents
description: Bot operators now have a home in the Cloudflare dashboard to manage submissions. This update adds submission status tracking, submission editing, and a behavior model so operators can accurately declare how their bots use content.

title: Post-Quantum Authentication: Up Next
description: Post-quantum key establishment has moved from standards into deployment. Post-quantum authentication has not moved nearly as far, and specification work is no longer the only constraint. The IAB is holding a workshop in Prague on 11 and 12 October 2026 to bring deployment experie…

title: How we saved 100 terabytes of memory by optimizing 1.1.1.1’s DNS cache
description: Five Rust-level memory optimizations to the DNS cache layout of Big Pineapple cut per-entry memory by 56%, freeing approximately 100 TB of memory across Cloudflare's fleet.

title: IETF 126 post-meeting survey: what we heard
description: The IETF 126 Vienna meeting was held 18-24 July 2026 and the results of the post-meeting survey are now available.

title: The Cloudflare Blog — brought to you by EmDash
description: We migrated the Cloudflare Blog to EmDash to prove our stack at massive scale. Here is how we stress-tested performance, safely routed production traffic, and redesigned the frontend experience.

title: DNS Abuse and Criminal Infrastructure: Beyond Definitions and Blocklists
description: Evidence suggests that criminals may control a substantial share of new gTLD registrations. Although the precise scale remains contested, the article asks whether current DNS Abuse measures adequately address wider misuse of domain names.

title: Say it once: Introducing Bot Preference Sync
description: Cloudflare's new Bot Preference Sync automatically aligns your robots.txt file with your AI bot policies for Search, Agent, and Training. Easily manage which bots access your content without maintaining static files.

title: From all-or-nothing to task-based OAuth consent
description: Cloudflare OAuth now supports optional scopes, giving users more control over what an app can access and helping developers build secure consent flows around the task at hand.

title: Deploying IPv6-first EKS on AWS: What Still Doesn't Work, and What It Saves
description: In this field report on IPv6-first Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS), the isp6 team shares which dependencies still drag IPv4 back in, what they learnt from /28s, and why the saving is large but not automatic.

title: Multiple LIR Accounts: Looking Back and Thinking Ahead
description: Why a feature introduced for a handful of members became one of the RIPE NCC's most complex operational challenges.

title: Make the Switch to More Secure API Key Handling for Reg-RWS
description: ARIN now supports sending your Reg-RWS API key through a header instead of a URL query parameter — a small change that closes off a real source of accidental credential exposure. Here's why it matters and how to make the switch.

title: Meet our new IETF NOC Lead
description: Joe Clarke has been appointed as the new IETF Network Operations Center (NOC) Lead and in this post Joe introduces himself and sets out his priorities for the IETF Network.

title: The State of IPv6 in the Caribbean
description: It's time for our annual update on who’s leading the charge for IPv6 adoption in the Caribbean, featuring new leaders and new lessons emerging from this year’s data.

title: Your Number Resource Record Is a Part of the Internet's Infrastructure — Respect It Like One
description: Legacy IPv4 Internet number resource holders: Is your registration data still doing its job? Nearly half of ARIN's legacy networks have no validated Point of Contact. Find out why that matters, and how to fix it in minutes.

title: Two Providers, a Stubborn Plateau and a Very Long Tail: Email in the Tranco Top-1M
description: Ten years of DNS measurements reveal three trends across the Internet's most popular domains: email continues to consolidate around two providers, DMARC enforcement has hit a plateau, and a surprisingly large long tail of infrastructure defies easy classification.

title: Secretariat restructuring and staffing update
description: There have been a few changes in IETF Administration LLC staffing since January of this year (2026) including the recent insourcing of the Secretariat, which are summarised here to give an overall view of the staffing structure.

title: What's ARP Got to Do with It?
description: It's only ARP. It works. So how much can it really matter? The answer lies beyond ARP itself, in the IPv4 layer cake that grew around it over four decades. The IPv4 internet is not going away in bounded time, and nobody should pretend otherwise.

title: Don’t Get Your Wires Crossed: Appropriate Use Cases for IPv6-Only vs. IPv6-Mostly
description: Terms like IPv6-only and IPv6-mostly are a clear example of how IETF terminology often lacks clarity. IPv6 expert Jordi Palet Martínez, explains why the correct use of these terms requires specifying a scope of application.

title: IETF Community Survey 2025
description: The IETF Community Survey provides a comprehensive assessment of community demographics, engagement patterns, and perceptions of organizational effectiveness. Read the full findings below.

title: Apply Today for the ARIN 58 Fellowship Program
description: The call for applications to our ARIN 58 Fellowship Program is out, and Senior Project Manager Amanda Gauldin shares more about what you can expect in this program, why you should consider applying, and what past Fellows have to say about the experience.

title: Birds of a Feather at IETF 126
description: The IETF 126 Vienna meeting takes place 18–24 July 2026. As at every IETF meeting, alongside the established Working Groups there will be a handful of Birds-of-a-Feather (BoF) sessions—and these are often the most interesting place to watch where Internet standards work is headin…

title: From Lab to RFC: A PhD Student's Journey through the IETF
description: Martine Sophie Lenders has been regularly participating in the IETF for over a decade, starting with the IETF 93 meeting in Prague in 2015. She has authored several Internet-Drafts—two of which recently were published as RFCs—and at the same time works on a PhD at FU Berlin and a…

title: ARIN Bits: June 2026
description: As temperatures rise, so does the momentum at ARIN. Dive into the summer edition of ARIN Bits for updates from our second quarter and details about upcoming items, including: the 2026 ARIN Elections cycle; fee and security changes; useful tools; reminders from Registration Servic…

title: Suggested IETF 126 Sessions for Getting Familiar with New Topics
description: These IETF 126 meeting sessions are likely to include discussions and proposals that are accessible to a broad range of Internet technologists whether they are new to the IETF or long-time participants.

title: Bridging Policy and Operations: An ARIN 57 Fellowship Experience
description: Read how the ARIN Fellowship Program strengthened this new community member's understanding of Internet governance and policy development and provided a meaningful forum in which to contribute ideas around routing security, automation, AI-assisted validation, and modernized polic…

title: Ready to Run? Your Guide to ARIN Elections Nominations
description: Who can make nominations? What should a nominee expect during the election timeline? How are nominees classified, and what qualifications matter most? Whether you’re considering running or simply want to understand ARIN Elections, this overview covers the essentials.
